_schema.title: Krinner et al., Nature 605, 669 (2022), arXiv:2112.03708: device calibration
_schema.readme: Every leaf quantity is an object {value, units, kind, source, uncertainty, measurement_run[, method]}. kind: 'published' (printed number in a paper), 'digitized' (read from a figure: the source names figure/panel/page), 'fitted' (computed by our numpy models: 'method' says how). uncertainty: {sigma, units[, basis/note]} as 1 sigma, or null when no estimate exists. measurement_run: a key of 'measurement_runs'. Units are SI (Hz, s); flux in flux quanta. Coupling convention: g_11_20 = sqrt(2) J_qq. Top-level sections: measurement_runs, coupling, qubits (per-qubit circuit values, flux_quanta_capable flag), flux_line (Hellings 2025 distortion model), cz (per-pair published values + knobs), crosstalk, defects, readout. Published values here duplicate the quantum system only where a calibration consumer needs them alongside fitted values; the quantum system remains the source of truth for published numbers.

measurement_runs.2022-main: the cooldown of Krinner22 Tab. I (columns without superscript a) and the QEC data
measurement_runs.2022-a: the other cooldown of the same device marked (a) in Krinner22 Tab. I; also Fig. 10 (drive crosstalk)
measurement_runs.2022-dephasing-run: Krinner22 App. E3 measurement-induced dephasing run (X1 parked at 4.429 GHz); cooldown not stated
measurement_runs.2025-flux-tuning: the cooldown of Hellings 2025 (X2 tuning curve, flux-line model, X2 CZ at 4.4 GHz); same device
measurement_runs.2025-lower-sweet-spot: the later cooldown of Remm et al., Phys. Rev. Research 8, 013044 (2026), arXiv:2502.17722, App. D Tab. I (X1 at its lower sweet spot); same device

coupling.convention: g_11_20 is the |11>-|20> matrix element at the interaction point (auxiliary first); J_qq = g_11_20 / sqrt(2) is the 0-1 exchange. Charge model: H_c = g_c n_A n_D.

g_11_20.source: Krinner et al., Nature 605, 669 (2022), arXiv:2112.03708v1, Methods A (p. 8) 'J/2pi ~ 7 MHz'; N. Lacroix, PhD thesis, ETH Zurich (2025), Diss. ETH No. 31121, doi:10.3929/ethz-b-000740393, §2.2.3 and §3.3.1 'sqrt(2) J_qq / 2pi ~ 7 MHz'
Hellings et al., arXiv:2503.04610 (2025), App. J (chevron fit, J_2/2pi = 7.4 MHz)
g_11_20.note: Hellings' partner is 'a 3.88 GHz neighbour' of X2: D4 (3.878) or D1 (3.885); stored on X2-D4, applies equally if it was X2-D1. Measured at omega_int = 4.4 GHz, not the Fig. 6c 5.276 GHz

calibration_A.source: Hellings et al., arXiv:2503.04610 (2025) App. J J_2 = 7.4 MHz
calibration_A.method: device-wide g_c such that the X2-D4 |11>-|20> half-splitting at 4.4 GHz is 7.4 MHz (5 levels each, no RWA)

calibration_B.source: Krinner et al., Nature 605, 669 (2022), arXiv:2112.03708v1 Methods A 'J ~ 7 MHz'
calibration_B.method: device-wide g_c such that the mean J_2 over the 24 published omega_int is 7.0 MHz

n_exponentials.source: Hellings et al., arXiv:2503.04610 (2025) §IV; N. Lacroix, PhD thesis, ETH Zurich (2025), Diss. ETH No. 31121, doi:10.3929/ethz-b-000740393, §3.3.1 ('typically N = 4')

fir.structure: L-tap FIR at T_s, regularized least-squares fit (Tikhonov + exponential tail; Sobolev regularization for the inverse) to a Gaussian target response of sigma = 0.75 ns

taps.source: Hellings et al., arXiv:2503.04610 (2025) App. I

fir.coefficients_status: not given in the cited sources

relative.source: Hellings et al., arXiv:2503.04610 (2025) §V (< 0.1 % of the step from 15 ns on)

knobs.description: Sudden-net-zero CZ (Negirneac et al., PRL 126, 220502 (2021)) as used on this device (N. Lacroix, PhD thesis, ETH Zurich (2025), Diss. ETH No. 31121, doi:10.3929/ethz-b-000740393, §2.2.3 and §3.3; Krinner et al., Nature 605, 669 (2022), arXiv:2112.03708v1 App. C1): two plateaus of duration t_p, sign-flipped in flux (same frequency), joined by a transition section of duration t_mid at amplitude B; Gaussian-filtered edges sigma = 0.5 ns (Hellings et al., arXiv:2503.04610 (2025) App. J). Knobs: duration, transition amplitude, amplitude offset.
knobs.units_note: amplitude offset is expressed as a detuning in Hz; B is a fraction of the plateau flux amplitude, meaningful because d is known for both qubits; Calibration.flux_for_detuning and detuning_for_flux convert detunings to flux quanta for qubits with flux_quanta_capable

duration_plateau.source: in-model calibration; omega_int from Krinner et al., Nature 605, 669 (2022), arXiv:2112.03708v1 Fig. 6c
duration_plateau.method: closed-system 2-transmon (5 levels each, charge basis, g_c n_A n_D, no RWA) piecewise-exact propagation; SNZ frequency trajectories with sigma = 0.5 ns Gaussian edges, t_mid = 6 samples (2.5 ns); durations on the 0.4167 ns grid; g_c per pair so that the |11>-|20> half-splitting equals the per-pair J_2 in coupling.model_j2_at_interaction (calibration_A g_c = 3.121 MHz, 7.28-9.55 MHz at the published omega_int); X2-D4 uses its Hellings override, which is the same calibration_A g_c; data-qubit transition flux from the Fig. 1c SQUID fit; step 1: half-pulse |11>->|20> transfer error minimised over delta for t_p around n0 = round(1/(4 J_2)/T_s) (window extended until interior); step 2: on the two best t_p, 41-point B scan in [0, 1] (extended to (1, 2] when phi_c does not reach 180 deg), Nelder-Mead on (delta, B) with cost log10(leakage from |11>) + (phi_c - 180 deg)^2/deg^2 from every 180-deg crossing and from delta +- 1 MHz; selection: |phi_c - 180| <= 1 deg, minimum leakage, smaller B on ties (within 2x, both < 1e-4); verified at dt = 2.5 ps
duration_plateau.limitations: closed system (no T1, T2, flux noise or TLS); ideal flux line (no residual distortion after IIR/FIR compensation, no crosstalk); no spectators (two transmons only, 5 levels each); omega_int digitized to +-10 MHz, so delta is re-found in-model; coupling from g_11_20 only (no per-pair capacitance)

transition_amplitude_B.limitations: closed system (no T1, T2, flux noise or TLS); ideal flux line (no residual distortion after IIR/FIR compensation, no crosstalk); no spectators (two transmons only, 5 levels each); omega_int digitized to +-10 MHz, so delta is re-found in-model; coupling from g_11_20 only (no per-pair capacitance)

defects.note: defects rearrange on every thermal cycle (Colao Zanuz 2024): valid for 2022-main only

uncertainty.note: frequency ±2 px; loss is clipped at 25 % (column width); rows within 3 px of a coloured line are masked, so a defect under a line is missed; scan_range_ghz_UNRELIABLE: zero-loss rows have no grey fill, so the trace extent is fragmented - use Fig. 1c for tuning ranges; broad comb-like loss (D7, X1) is reported only by its strongest peaks

feedlines.source: Krinner22 arXiv:2112.03708v1 Fig. 1b (page 2), false-colour micrograph; rasters png/fig1b_300.png and png/fig1b_tr_600.png
feedlines.method: Visual trace of the purple feedlines to the blue Purcell filters at 300/600 dpi (top-left feedline traced: Z1 and D4 filters directly, D7/Z2 filters by proximity), then the remaining qubits partitioned by chip quadrant and checked against Methods B: 4 feedlines of 4-5 qubits with readout resonators ~200 MHz apart within a feedline. Every in-feedline spacing in this partition is >= 150 MHz; uniqueness was checked only for X3 (X3 with Z3 would be 58 MHz apart).

top_left.confidence: high for Z1, D4 (traced); medium for D7, Z2

top_right.confidence: medium (X2-D5 published; rest by quadrant + spacing)

bottom_left.confidence: medium (D9 published; rest by quadrant + spacing)

cross_checks: X2 and D5 share a feedline: Remm 2023 (TWPA, arXiv:2210.04799) App. F - satisfied
D9 is on the 'bottom-left' feedline: Swiadek 2024 (arXiv:2307.07765) Fig. 7 - satisfied (orientation as in Fig. 1b)
